title: Restore prompt-fanout throughput and TTFT for multi-variant models (customer escalations)
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: Over the last 36 hours multiple customers reported severe first-token-latency (TTFT) regressions and tokens/sec collapse when their prompts performed wide model fanout (2-6 variants). The regression appears across Hosted, Dedicated and Private deployments. Initial telemetry points to an interaction between the kernel selection heuristic and aggressive KV-prefetch scheduling that caused: 1) oversized prefetches that saturated GPU memory transiently, 2) eviction churn in the KV cache, and 3) a backlog at the serving head that amplified on short-lived burst traffic (prompt fanout + multi-turn contexts).

Repro: Synthetic replay with 60 concurrent short prompts that fanout to 4 variant copies reproduces 2-3x TTFT increase and tokens/sec drop to 20% of baseline. Heap/gpu-utils show transient memory pressure spikes around prefetch/compile boundaries.

Impact: Several paying customers reported degraded SLAs (not meeting 95p TTFT), user-facing timeouts, and increased error rates when fallback logic triggered. A customer with reserved Dedicated capacity observed throughput collapse for a 12 min window before the existing shedder engaged.

Immediate mitigation performed: See comments for timeline. High-level mitigation applied was: narrowed kernel-selection to "compat-mode" fallback for variants with >512 prefix tokens, limited prefetch concurrency to 2 inflight per GPU, and enabled a local per-tenant prefetch quota. These steps restored baseline TTFT for canary traffic but require a code patch and controlled rollout.

Goal: Ship a targeted runtime patch that: (a) prevents oversized prefetch batches from causing eviction churn, (b) adds a lightweight KV-prefetch circuit-breaker (per-model and per-tenant), (c) hardens kernel-selection against spurious compile thrashing in multi-variant fanout, and (d) roll out with canary + staged ramp to all environments with observability and cutover plan.

Acceptance criteria: 
- TTFT 95p for the affected customers returns to baseline within 15% at 95p for 72h post-rollout.
- Tokens/sec on busy fanout workloads recovers to >=90% of baseline.
- No increase in error rate or OOMs across Hosted/Dedicated/Private during canary.

Rollout plan: patch -> internal canary (10% traffic small subset customers) -> staged ramp (50% -> 100%) over 6 hours with automated rollback triggers in Console (TTFT delta >25% or error rate >1.5x).

Artifacts and links:
- Incident dashboard: https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/incident/INC-2026-03-10-prompt-fanout
- Repro harness + logs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/repro-harness/pulls/274
- Candidate runtime PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1832
- Runbook (temporary mitigations & rollback procedures): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OPS/Prompt+Fanout+TTFT+Incident
- Postmortem stub: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OPS/PM-FANOUT-POSTMORTEM
